solution:
The measure of the central angle of a sector is proportional to the number of scores in its component:

\(\theta = \dfrac{\text{Number of scores in the component}}{\text{Total number of scores}} \times 360^\circ\)

Here the O- group is 40 % of the persons, so

\(\theta = \dfrac{40}{100} \times 360^\circ = 144^\circ\)

\(\therefore\) the measure of the angle is \(144^\circ\) — the fourth alternative.

(This agrees with the answer printed at the back of the book.)

solution:
Let the total expenditure be ₹ \(x\). The cement sector's central angle is proportional to its share of the expenditure:

\(75 = \dfrac{45000}{x} \times 360\)

\(\therefore x = \dfrac{45000 \times 360}{75} = 45000 \times 4.8 = 216000\)

\(\therefore\) the total expenditure of the construction was ₹ 2,16,000 — the first alternative.

(This agrees with the answer printed at the back of the book.)

solution:
The chapter builds a 'less than' cumulative frequency column in order to locate the class that contains the \(\dfrac{N}{2}\)th score — the median class — and the median formula \(L + \left[\dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\right] \times h\) uses \(cf\) directly.

The mean is found from \(x_i f_i\) (or from deviations) and the mode from \(f_0, f_1, f_2\); neither uses cumulative frequency.

\(\therefore\) cumulative frequencies are useful to find the median — the second alternative.

(This agrees with the answer printed at the back of the book.)

solution:
In the step deviation method the chapter defines the deviation \(d_i = x_i - A\) and then divides it by the common factor \(g\):

\(u_i = \dfrac{d_i}{g} = \dfrac{x_i - A}{g}\)

\(\therefore u_i = \dfrac{x_i - A}{g}\) — the third alternative.

(This agrees with the answer printed at the back of the book.)

\(N = 11 + 12 + 20 + 7 = 50\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 25\).

The 'less than' cumulative frequencies are 11, 23, 43, 50. The 25th score is the first one past 23, so it lies in the third class.

\(\therefore\) the median lies in the group 16-18 — the third alternative.

solution:
A frequency polygon is plotted with the CLASS MARK as the \(x\)-coordinate and the frequency as the \(y\)-coordinate.

The classes 1-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10-12 are discontinuous, but making them continuous does not change a class mark, so the class mark of 4-6 is \(\dfrac{4 + 6}{2} = 5\), and its frequency is 8.

\(\therefore\) the coordinates are (5, 8) — the third alternative.

(This agrees with the answer printed at the back of the book.)
